inicial.meta_descricao: Carbono Consciente: environmental education on carbon emissions, carbon footprint, sustainable tips, fun facts and environmental news.

hero.titulo: Every small habit weighs less on the planet
hero.texto: CARBONO CONSCIENTE IS NOT A GREEN SEAL OR A DISTANT GOAL — IT'S THE SUM OF ORDINARY CHOICES, REPEATED EVERY DAY: WHAT YOU PLANT, HOW YOU GET AROUND, WHEN YOU TURN OFF THE LIGHT, WHERE YOU THROW YOUR TRASH.

acordeao.emissao_corpo: Carbon emission is the release of gases such as CO₂ into the atmosphere, mainly from burning fossil fuels, deforestation, industrial production and even everyday transportation.
acordeao.clima_titulo: How does it affect the climate?
acordeao.clima_corpo: Greenhouse gases form a layer that traps heat in the atmosphere. The more emissions, the stronger this effect — and that's what drives global warming and climate change.
acordeao.pegada_corpo: It's the total amount of greenhouse gases generated, directly or indirectly, by the activities of a person, company or product in their day-to-day life.
acordeao.neutro_corpo: Carbon neutral seeks to balance or offset the emissions generated. Carbono consciente prioritizes choices that reduce environmental impact before even thinking about offsetting.

fatos.fato1: An adult tree absorbs, on average, about 22 kg of CO₂ per year — which is why reforestation is one of the most direct ways to offset emissions.
fatos.fato2: The oceans absorb about a quarter of all the CO₂ humanity emits every year, acting as a huge regulator of the global climate.
fatos.fato3: Recycling one tonne of paper saves about 17 trees and a significant amount of water and energy compared to producing new paper.
fatos.fato4: Transportation is responsible for about a quarter of global energy-related CO₂ emissions — swapping the car for a bike or public transport on short trips makes a real difference.
fatos.fato5: The Amazon is home to about 10% of all known biodiversity on the planet, as well as storing billions of tonnes of carbon in its vegetation.
fatos.fato6: Residential solar panels can cut a household's carbon footprint by tonnes of CO₂ per year, depending on the local energy mix.
fatos.fato7: A diet with less red meat can significantly reduce a person's carbon footprint, since cattle farming is one of the most emissions-intensive agricultural activities.
fatos.fato8: Melting Arctic sea ice reduces the planet's ability to reflect sunlight back into space, accelerating warming — an effect known as albedo feedback.
fatos.fato9: LED bulbs use up to 80% less energy than incandescent bulbs and last much longer, cutting both emissions and waste.
fatos.fato10: The Paris Agreement, signed by nearly 200 countries, aims to limit global warming to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels.
fatos.fato11: About a third of all food produced in the world is wasted — and that waste alone generates a significant share of global greenhouse gas emissions.
fatos.fato12: Modern wind turbines can generate enough energy to power thousands of homes, without emitting CO₂ during operation.
fatos.fato13: Healthy soil stores more carbon than all vegetation and the atmosphere combined — regenerative farming practices help keep that carbon in the ground.
fatos.fato14: Coral reefs, despite covering less than 1% of the ocean floor, support about 25% of all known marine life — and are extremely sensitive to warming waters.
fatos.fato15: Cutting hot water waste at home (shorter showers, for example) also reduces emissions, since heating water takes energy.
fatos.fato16: Electric cars, even accounting for battery manufacturing, tend to emit less CO₂ over their lifetime than combustion cars, especially where electricity comes from clean sources.
fatos.fato17: Composting organic waste at home keeps it from producing methane in landfills — a greenhouse gas far more potent than CO₂ in the short term.
fatos.fato18: Greenland and Antarctica's glaciers together have been losing hundreds of billions of tonnes of ice per year in recent years, directly contributing to sea level rise.
